title: Flavin and Cherono Win the 2025 Marathon Project
excerpt: JP Flavin came from behind to win the 2025 Marathon Project in 2:09:18; Priscah Cherono, 45, won in 2:25:17. What their races show about pacing.
body:
At the Marathon Project in Chandler, Arizona, on December 21, 2025, JP Flavin of Hansons-Brooks won the men's race in a personal best of 2:09:18. Paul Chelimo and Nadeel Wildschutt pushed the pace, but Flavin came from behind to win. Turner Wiley was second in 2:09:27, and Wildschutt third in 2:09:40 in his debut.

Kenya's Priscah Cherono, 45, won the women's race in 2:25:17, more than three minutes ahead of Molly Grabill (2:28:56).

Flavin's win is a reminder that you don't have to go with the leaders to win the race. In a marathon, the runners who keep an even pace often pass those who went out too hard.

Look at your own splits after every race. Aim for an even pace, or a second half only slightly slower than the first, and practise it in long runs before you try it on race day.

Sources: LetsRun.com results; LetsRun.com race report
keyTakeaway: You don't need to go with the leaders early; an even pace often wins the second half.
